implemented: Fixed two-feed configuration; public-only DNS resolution is pinned to direct TLS connections with certificate/SNI verification, 10-second timeout, redirects rejected, XML MIME and 1 MiB response limits, UTF-8-only RSS/Atom parsing, DTD/ENTITY and malformed/root validation, 50-entry cap, and visible excluded off-host links.

Schema version 2 creates discovery candidate/check tables without rebuilding or deleting existing operator project records. Exact-URL dedupe preserves first_seen and status; title+URL snapshot hash and source-stated date remain separate; failed checks retain prior candidates and expose per-feed errors.

Protected empty-body-shape POST /api/discovery/check, searchable GET /api/discovery, protected candidate status changes and explicit /admit action. Admission creates the project with UNKNOWN project evidence and links candidate atomically; retries return the same project.

Operator UI uses text nodes for feed content, safe external links, per-feed status/counts, reversible dismissal, explicit project title/location/phase entry, independent candidate scrolling, and clear on-demand two-feed coverage wording.
Reject future-dated conversation records so they cannot represent completed customer contact or satisfy downstream gates.
Quickstart documents both installed entrypoint and non-disruptive source launch for the existing running-executable lock condition.
limitations: Live-source checking, browser intake/admission, package/runtime proof, repository-wide gates, and integrated independent review are controller-owned and pending.
Only the two specified feeds are checked; candidates are unqualified signals and do not establish power need, buyer authority, or customer engagement.
No background scheduler, article crawler, or external sending is implemented.
authority: No commit, push, merge, deployment, external communication, or production database operation. The user's live .trailforge-operator.sqlite3 data was not opened or altered.
